rules.reason: R-source-timing documents source reuse and per-attempt subscriptions; R-history-view and F-view-owner distinguish visit identities. No unsupported ownership policy.

R-task and R-source-timing require a receiver to be eligible for the synchronous initial emission. F-progress documents the defective ordering; current defect is not preserved as policy. No unique API is required.

R-history-view forbids new events after retirement without a grace period; F-navigation and F-cancel show handles/removers arrive after startup. I-startup-window connects that timing to the observed traces. Immediate loss of admission eligibility is independent of eventual physical cleanup; no blanket cancellation policy.

R-history-view explicitly retains exactly-once audit when previously admitted decoding finishes after closing. F-view-owner separates retained record from current display. No suppression of accepted audit or permission for new retired admission.

R-reentry and R-retry-entry retain newer ownership and entry-bound commands under synchronous callbacks. F-navigation/F-cancel/F-retry provide actual placement. Rule preserves behavior without mandating one implementation.

R-source-timing and R-history-view permit synchronous emission/reentry; O-dev traces show retired audit before old startup returns. F-dev1-selfchecks confirms the old-source follow-up emit occurs only after outer select returns, leaving this window unchecked. F-dev2-selfchecks and scores support checking visibility separately; outcomes do not establish isolated causation.
R-task and R-format exclude record/interface extension; R-reentry/R-source-timing preserve existing retry/cancel, independent owners and shared source. No business expansion.
